question: What anatomical structure forms the anterior boundary of the vulva?
explanation: The mons pubis sits over the pubic bone at the front, marking the upper or anterior limit of the vulva. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h1)

question: During a normal delivery, a midwife checks a tear near the back part of the vulva. Which structure is most likely involved?
explanation: The perineal body forms the posterior boundary of the vulva and is the most common site for tears during childbirth. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which skin folds lie directly inside the labia majora and enclose the vestibule?
explanation: The labia minora are the inner folds of skin that frame the vestibule and protect the vaginal and urethral openings. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h2)

question: What happens when Bartholin's glands become infected or blocked?

options.A: They regulate the structural support of the pubic symphysis
options.B: They produce excessive pubic hair during pregnancy
options.C: They reside in the vestibule and can form painful cysts or abscesses
options.D: They directly control the hormonal cycle of menstruation

explanation: The ducts of Bartholin's glands open into the vestibule, and blockage of these ducts leads to painful fluid accumulation and infection. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which main blood vessel is the primary source of arterial blood to the vulva?
explanation: The internal pudendal artery supplies most of the blood to the external genitalia. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why does a superficial tear on the vulva during delivery often swell up very quickly?

options.A: Lymphatic vessels dilate rapidly to absorb amniotic fluid
options.B: Arterial pressure in the pelvis drops sharply during the second stage
options.C: Skeletal muscles in the perineum contract continuously
options.D: The vulva contains a dense network of blood vessels and erectile tissue

explanation: The rich vascular network and erectile tissue in the vulva lead to fast bleeding and hematoma formation when injured. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h3)

question: Where does the majority of lymphatic fluid from the vulva drain to first?
explanation: The superficial inguinal nodes in the groin are the primary destination for vulvar lymph drainage. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h4)

question: A patient has an infected wound on the labia majora. Which lymph nodes should the midwife check first?
explanation: Because the labia majora drain directly to the superficial inguinal nodes, infection in this area commonly causes groin node enlargement. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which nerve provides the main sensation and movement to the perineum?
explanation: The pudendal nerve (S2-S4) is the primary nerve supplying the perineal structures. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why is a pudendal nerve block helpful for pain relief during an instrumental vaginal delivery?

options.A: It blocks parasympathetic impulses to the urinary bladder
options.B: It relaxes the smooth muscle fibres inside the uterine body
options.C: It numbs the somatic sensory fibers supplying the lower vagina and perineum
options.D: It stops sympathetic vasoconstriction in the femoral vessels

explanation: Blocking the pudendal nerve desensitizes the perineal tissues, providing excellent pain relief for repairs and instrumental births. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h5)

question: What causes the bluish discoloration of the vulva and vagina observed during early pregnancy?

options.A: Chronic inflammation of the Bartholin's ducts
options.C: Melanin deposition from rising estrogen levels
options.D: Decreased cardiac output to the lower extremities

explanation: The extra blood flow and congestion in pregnancy create a bluish hue known as Chadwick's sign. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h6)

question: A postpartum woman has severe, throbbing perineal pain a few hours after a normal delivery, even though her stitches are intact. What condition should the midwife suspect?
explanation: Severe, disproportionate perineal pain with swelling often indicates hidden bleeding into the tissues, forming a hematoma. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T1#BMP210_U2_T1_h6)
